requests.change: Rewrite the epoch mechanism per delegated rulings R13/R14 (re-mark touched R1 text "delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14"; marker *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14)*; in-text record "Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14 (user delegated all remaining calls, including naming the reference machine)"). New names, used identically in every file: `slot_epoch.bin`, `slot_epoch.tmp`, `EPOCH_DURABLE`, `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` (replaces `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`), `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`, `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500, unchanged), `t_epoch_wait`. (A) SL-23 (1)-(5) replacement text: "(1) *Advance (R13).* A death-stub restore (`DEATH_STUB`) always advances `restore_epoch`. A Continue (`LOAD_GAME`, in-process or in a fresh process) or a `FAULT_RECOVERY` restore advances it unless the generation it restores is a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation; that Continue carries the epoch unchanged and writes nothing (user ruling D16, 'not steerable by quit', outranks R1). An advance sets `restore_epoch := min(2^32 − 1, max(e_mem, e_slot) + 1)`, `e_slot` the value in `slot_epoch.bin`, `e_mem` the in-memory value; at 2^32 − 1 it saturates and logs. A stub that finds nothing loadable restores nothing and does not advance it. (2) *Durable before the restore is requested (R14).* `restore_epoch` lives in the per-slot side file `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch.bin` (u32 little-endian + CRC32, 8 bytes), written by the Save/Load worker atomically (`slot_epoch.tmp`, flush, rename over, re-read with a valid CRC = `EPOCH_DURABLE`). It is in no generation file, so no generation's bytes, trailer SHA-256 or any key derived from them (SL-12) ever change after `VERIFYING`. When an advance is due, Save/Load runs a pre-restore staging step: after selection, pre-check and staging (SL-8, SL-11) it hands the new value to the worker, polls once per frame (never blocking the main thread), and calls `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`; the kernel's `LOADING` stays atomic within one boundary service. For the death stub the kernel keeps running between the `DEAD` boundary and that call (`t_epoch_wait`, F-8, typically one frame): the seat stays `DEAD`, the hard gate is closed (a seat `DEAD`, a restore pending), Save/Load issues no snapshot and no pause, the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame, and every tick of that interval is discarded by the restore. For a Continue the staging runs behind the Continue press, before the kernel is touched. (2a) *Failure path, a listed exposure.* If the write fails or `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` passes, the restore proceeds with the advanced value in memory, `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` is logged and `save_status` is set to `FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway); the worker re-attempts the `slot_epoch.bin` write with the next write job; a kill before a later successful write may replay that epoch once (OQ-25). (2b) *Recovery copy.* Each generation header records the live `restore_epoch` at write time (SL-1) and is never rewritten. A missing `slot_epoch.bin`, or one failing its CRC32, reads as `max(the newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`, and is rewritten at the next advance. `new_game` writes `slot_epoch.bin` = 0 (SL-18)." (3) keeps its content with the new signature. (4) unchanged. (5) -> "the player can neither pick nor predict the new value; a death re-keys the next stretch (metric M2); a Save & Quit then Continue carries the epoch, so the threat draws after Continue are those the quitting session would have met — quit buys no re-key (R13; OQ-50 closed); a kill then Continue of an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation advances it, priced by the minutes lost since that autosave (OQ-25). The former rules 'advances on a death-stub restore only' and 'every restore advances it' are superseded." Delete "is a key of every generation header (SL-1), so it survives ...", every `E_seen` definition and use, and the whole header-only rewrite / end-of-`LOADING` `EPOCH_DURABLE` wait text. Wall-clock paragraph: add `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` to the monotonic I/O timeouts and note it is the one that runs while `T` advances (the dead-world interval of the death stub), changing no sim state. (B) States intro: "which is persisted in the generation headers (SL-23)" -> "which is persisted in `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-23, R14), with a write-time copy in each generation header". (C) SL-1 `restore_epoch` header row: "The campaign's restore counter (SL-23): the value live when this file was last written, raised by 1 on every restore by an atomic header-only rewrite of the restored generation" -> "A write-time recovery copy of the campaign's `restore_epoch` (SL-23): the value live when this generation was written; never rewritten (R14); read only when `slot_epoch.bin` is missing or fails its CRC32"; "It is sim-visible through `kernel.clock`, so it is a behaviour-changing field" -> "It can reach the sim through the recovery rule, so it stays a behaviour-changing field". (D) SL-19 directory list: add "`slot_epoch.bin` (the slot's `restore_epoch`, u32 + CRC32, SL-23) and its transient `slot_epoch.tmp`". (E) SL-7: replace "Save/Load then bumps `write_epoch` (SL-10), computes `restore_epoch` (SL-23), selects a generation (SL-8), pre-checks and stages it (SL-11), ... and only then calls `request_restore(payload)`, which the kernel honours at that tick's boundary services" with "Save/Load then bumps `write_epoch` (SL-10), selects a generation (SL-8), pre-checks and stages it (SL-11, hot copy where one exists), computes the advanced `restore_epoch` and hands its `slot_epoch.bin` write to the worker (SL-23 (2)), and calls `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` at the first boundary after `EPOCH_DURABLE` (or `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`), typically the next tick's; the kernel honours it at that boundary's services (the Controller's `DEAD` row and Edge Case conform, R14)"; Sequence -> "`DEAD` → (same boundary: write settled or abandoned, `write_epoch`++, generation selected, pre-checked and staged, epoch write issued) → (per-frame poll; the dead world ticks with the hard gate closed and the down sheet's last frame held) → `EPOCH_DURABLE` → `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` → kernel `LOADING` ..."; the cut-channel sentence "the request is made at the tick's boundary" -> "the stub starts at the tick's boundary and the request follows its epoch staging". (F) SL-11: "the `DEAD` tick only selects and hands over" -> "the `DEAD` tick only selects, stages and issues the epoch write"; "before `request_restore(payload)` is issued" -> "before the epoch staging step and `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` (SL-23 (2))". (G) T-6 intro: delete "The scan also computes `E_seen` (SL-23) from every header that parses, and two verifying files with the same `generation` (a header-only epoch rewrite ...) are ordered by `restore_epoch`, the higher winning; ..." -> "The scan also checks `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-23 (2b)): a leftover `slot_epoch.tmp` is deleted (its rename never happened, and no restore used its value, because `request_restore` waits for `EPOCH_DURABLE`); a missing or CRC-failing `slot_epoch.bin` is rebuilt by the recovery rule." Add table row: "During the `slot_epoch` write | `slot_epoch.bin` (old value) intact and a `slot_epoch.tmp` | Delete the `.tmp`; the old value stands". (H) T-8: intro add "the epoch staging step runs between the `DEAD` boundary and the request (SL-23 (2))"; step 2: replace "then `write_epoch`++ and `restore_epoch` computed and its header-only rewrite queued to the worker (SL-23)" with "then `write_epoch`++" and append after staging "then the advanced `restore_epoch` is computed and its `slot_epoch.bin` write handed to the worker (SL-23 (2))"; new step 2b | each following frame boundary | Save/Load | "Polls the epoch write; the kernel stays `RUNNING` with the seat `DEAD`, the hard gate closed and the down sheet's last frame held; no request is issued until `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` with `save_status` = `FAILED` after `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS`"; step 3 Tick boundary -> "The first boundary after step 2b completes", Result -> "`request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` of the staged WORLD blocks"; step 4 -> "That boundary's services"; step 7 Result -> "`restore_reason = DEATH_STUB` published; the verdict from the kernel's K-4 report (SL-12); the kernel enters `RUNNING`" (delete the `EPOCH_DURABLE` wait). (I) F-8: formula -> "`restart_ms = LOAD_ATTEMPTS × precheck_ms + t_epoch_wait + max(loading_ms, t_hold_pad)`; `t_epoch_wait = 0` when no advance is due (a Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation, R13), else `frame_ms × ceil(min(t_epoch, RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS) / frame_ms)`, `frame_ms = 1000 / TICK_RATE` = 16.7"; `t_epoch` row -> "1 … `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` [UNV] | worker | the `slot_epoch.bin` write (temp, flush, rename, re-read), before `request_restore`"; add `t_epoch_wait` row (float ms, 0 or 16.7 … 500, calculated, 'the per-frame-polled wait before the request; for the stub the down sheet's last frame is held through it, for a Continue the menu shows it; it precedes the black hold'). Output Range: "`max(loading_ms, t_hold_pad, t_epoch)` is the black hold" -> "`max(loading_ms, t_hold_pad)` is the black hold; `t_epoch_wait` precedes it". Example (t_epoch = 4 ms [UNV], one poll frame, t_epoch_wait = 16.7): "`restart_ms = 1 × 19.7 + 16.7 + max(6.1, 120) = 156.4 ms` ≤ 1 000 ✓ (hot copy: 16.7 + 16.7 + 120 = 153.4); worst case, two candidates refused: 3 × 19.7 + 16.7 + 120 = 59.1 + 16.7 + 120 = 195.8 ms; a Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation (no advance): 19.7 + 0 + 120 = 139.7 and 59.1 + 0 + 120 = 179.1; at the epoch timeout: 19.7 + 30 × 16.67 (= 500) + 120 = 639.7 ms ≤ 1 000 ✓". (J) Tuning knob row `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS`: too high -> "the pre-restore staging stretches (the held down-sheet frame, or the Continue screen) while a slow disk finishes the `slot_epoch.bin` write"; too low -> "the write is declared not durable (`SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, `save_status` `FAILED`) on a healthy slow disk; a kill before the next successful write replays that epoch once"; affects -> "SL-23 (2), (2a); T-8 step 2b; F-8 `t_epoch_wait`; monotonic ms". (K) Player Fantasy anchor step 4: "On that same tick's boundary the death stub requests a restore of the newest verified generation (the one from T = 437 400)" -> "On that same tick's boundary the death stub selects and stages the newest verified generation (the one from T = 437 400) and makes the new restore epoch durable; at the next boundary, one frame later, it requests the restore (R14)". Player Fantasy D16 note: "(... the epoch advances on every restore, death stub or load, and is durable before the first `RUNNING` tick; whether a Save & Quit followed by Continue should instead be exempt is a USER DECISION, OQ-50.)" -> "(R13/R14: a death-stub restore advances the epoch and makes it durable before the restore is requested; a Continue of the newest Save & Quit generation carries it, so quitting buys no re-key; OQ-50 closed.)" Game Feel 'then on the `DEAD` tick the stub restores' -> 'then the stub starts on the `DEAD` tick and restores one frame later'. (L) Edge Cases: 'Continue while LOADING' "one `restore_epoch` step" -> "at most one `restore_epoch` step (none for a Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation, R13)"; 'DEAD during a camera cut' "the request is made at that tick's boundary" -> "the stub starts at that tick's boundary and the request follows its epoch staging (R14)". (M) Every Interactions/Dependencies row quoting the epoch as a header value or the old signature conforms to the wording above. G3 confirming grep after the edit: `header-only|E_seen|SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE|end-of-.LOADING. hand-off|every restore advances|advances on every restore|in the generation headers` -> zero hits outside history markers.

requests.anchor: SL-23 "(2) *Durable before play.* Save/Load durably writes the new value into the header of the generation it restores, by an atomic header-only rewrite"
requests.change: Rewrite the epoch mechanism per delegated rulings R13/R14 (re-mark touched R1 text "delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14"; marker *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14)*; in-text record "Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14 (user delegated all remaining calls, including naming the reference machine)"). New names, used identically in every file: `slot_epoch.bin`, `slot_epoch.tmp`, `EPOCH_DURABLE`, `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` (replaces `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`), `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`, `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500, unchanged), `t_epoch_wait`. (A) SL-23 (1)-(5) replacement text: "(1) *Advance (R13).* A death-stub restore (`DEATH_STUB`) always advances `restore_epoch`. A Continue (`LOAD_GAME`, in-process or in a fresh process) or a `FAULT_RECOVERY` restore advances it unless the generation it restores is a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation; that Continue carries the epoch unchanged and writes nothing (user ruling D16, 'not steerable by quit', outranks R1). An advance sets `restore_epoch := min(2^32 − 1, max(e_mem, e_slot) + 1)`, `e_slot` the value in `slot_epoch.bin`, `e_mem` the in-memory value; at 2^32 − 1 it saturates and logs. A stub that finds nothing loadable restores nothing and does not advance it. (2) *Durable before the restore is requested (R14).* `restore_epoch` lives in the per-slot side file `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch.bin` (u32 little-endian + CRC32, 8 bytes), written by the Save/Load worker atomically (`slot_epoch.tmp`, flush, rename over, re-read with a valid CRC = `EPOCH_DURABLE`). It is in no generation file, so no generation's bytes, trailer SHA-256 or any key derived from them (SL-12) ever change after `VERIFYING`. When an advance is due, Save/Load runs a pre-restore staging step: after selection, pre-check and staging (SL-8, SL-11) it hands the new value to the worker, polls once per frame (never blocking the main thread), and calls `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`; the kernel's `LOADING` stays atomic within one boundary service. For the death stub the kernel keeps running between the `DEAD` boundary and that call (`t_epoch_wait`, F-8, typically one frame): the seat stays `DEAD`, the hard gate is closed (a seat `DEAD`, a restore pending), Save/Load issues no snapshot and no pause, the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame, and every tick of that interval is discarded by the restore. For a Continue the staging runs behind the Continue press, before the kernel is touched. (2a) *Failure path, a listed exposure.* If the write fails or `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` passes, the restore proceeds with the advanced value in memory, `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` is logged and `save_status` is set to `FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway); the worker re-attempts the `slot_epoch.bin` write with the next write job; a kill before a later successful write may replay that epoch once (OQ-25). (2b) *Recovery copy.* Each generation header records the live `restore_epoch` at write time (SL-1) and is never rewritten. A missing `slot_epoch.bin`, or one failing its CRC32, reads as `max(the newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`, and is rewritten at the next advance. `new_game` writes `slot_epoch.bin` = 0 (SL-18)." (3) keeps its content with the new signature. (4) unchanged. (5) -> "the player can neither pick nor predict the new value; a death re-keys the next stretch (metric M2); a Save & Quit then Continue carries the epoch, so the threat draws after Continue are those the quitting session would have met — quit buys no re-key (R13; OQ-50 closed); a kill then Continue of an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation advances it, priced by the minutes lost since that autosave (OQ-25). The former rules 'advances on a death-stub restore only' and 'every restore advances it' are superseded." Delete "is a key of every generation header (SL-1), so it survives ...", every `E_seen` definition and use, and the whole header-only rewrite / end-of-`LOADING` `EPOCH_DURABLE` wait text. Wall-clock paragraph: add `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` to the monotonic I/O timeouts and note it is the one that runs while `T` advances (the dead-world interval of the death stub), changing no sim state. (B) States intro: "which is persisted in the generation headers (SL-23)" -> "which is persisted in `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-23, R14), with a write-time copy in each generation header". (C) SL-1 `restore_epoch` header row: "The campaign's restore counter (SL-23): the value live when this file was last written, raised by 1 on every restore by an atomic header-only rewrite of the restored generation" -> "A write-time recovery copy of the campaign's `restore_epoch` (SL-23): the value live when this generation was written; never rewritten (R14); read only when `slot_epoch.bin` is missing or fails its CRC32"; "It is sim-visible through `kernel.clock`, so it is a behaviour-changing field" -> "It can reach the sim through the recovery rule, so it stays a behaviour-changing field". (D) SL-19 directory list: add "`slot_epoch.bin` (the slot's `restore_epoch`, u32 + CRC32, SL-23) and its transient `slot_epoch.tmp`". (E) SL-7: replace "Save/Load then bumps `write_epoch` (SL-10), computes `restore_epoch` (SL-23), selects a generation (SL-8), pre-checks and stages it (SL-11), ... and only then calls `request_restore(payload)`, which the kernel honours at that tick's boundary services" with "Save/Load then bumps `write_epoch` (SL-10), selects a generation (SL-8), pre-checks and stages it (SL-11, hot copy where one exists), computes the advanced `restore_epoch` and hands its `slot_epoch.bin` write to the worker (SL-23 (2)), and calls `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` at the first boundary after `EPOCH_DURABLE` (or `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`), typically the next tick's; the kernel honours it at that boundary's services (the Controller's `DEAD` row and Edge Case conform, R14)"; Sequence -> "`DEAD` → (same boundary: write settled or abandoned, `write_epoch`++, generation selected, pre-checked and staged, epoch write issued) → (per-frame poll; the dead world ticks with the hard gate closed and the down sheet's last frame held) → `EPOCH_DURABLE` → `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` → kernel `LOADING` ..."; the cut-channel sentence "the request is made at the tick's boundary" -> "the stub starts at the tick's boundary and the request follows its epoch staging". (F) SL-11: "the `DEAD` tick only selects and hands over" -> "the `DEAD` tick only selects, stages and issues the epoch write"; "before `request_restore(payload)` is issued" -> "before the epoch staging step and `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` (SL-23 (2))". (G) T-6 intro: delete "The scan also computes `E_seen` (SL-23) from every header that parses, and two verifying files with the same `generation` (a header-only epoch rewrite ...) are ordered by `restore_epoch`, the higher winning; ..." -> "The scan also checks `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-23 (2b)): a leftover `slot_epoch.tmp` is deleted (its rename never happened, and no restore used its value, because `request_restore` waits for `EPOCH_DURABLE`); a missing or CRC-failing `slot_epoch.bin` is rebuilt by the recovery rule." Add table row: "During the `slot_epoch` write | `slot_epoch.bin` (old value) intact and a `slot_epoch.tmp` | Delete the `.tmp`; the old value stands". (H) T-8: intro add "the epoch staging step runs between the `DEAD` boundary and the request (SL-23 (2))"; step 2: replace "then `write_epoch`++ and `restore_epoch` computed and its header-only rewrite queued to the worker (SL-23)" with "then `write_epoch`++" and append after staging "then the advanced `restore_epoch` is computed and its `slot_epoch.bin` write handed to the worker (SL-23 (2))"; new step 2b | each following frame boundary | Save/Load | "Polls the epoch write; the kernel stays `RUNNING` with the seat `DEAD`, the hard gate closed and the down sheet's last frame held; no request is issued until `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` with `save_status` = `FAILED` after `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS`"; step 3 Tick boundary -> "The first boundary after step 2b completes", Result -> "`request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` of the staged WORLD blocks"; step 4 -> "That boundary's services"; step 7 Result -> "`restore_reason = DEATH_STUB` published; the verdict from the kernel's K-4 report (SL-12); the kernel enters `RUNNING`" (delete the `EPOCH_DURABLE` wait). (I) F-8: formula -> "`restart_ms = LOAD_ATTEMPTS × precheck_ms + t_epoch_wait + max(loading_ms, t_hold_pad)`; `t_epoch_wait = 0` when no advance is due (a Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation, R13), else `frame_ms × ceil(min(t_epoch, RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS) / frame_ms)`, `frame_ms = 1000 / TICK_RATE` = 16.7"; `t_epoch` row -> "1 … `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` [UNV] | worker | the `slot_epoch.bin` write (temp, flush, rename, re-read), before `request_restore`"; add `t_epoch_wait` row (float ms, 0 or 16.7 … 500, calculated, 'the per-frame-polled wait before the request; for the stub the down sheet's last frame is held through it, for a Continue the menu shows it; it precedes the black hold'). Output Range: "`max(loading_ms, t_hold_pad, t_epoch)` is the black hold" -> "`max(loading_ms, t_hold_pad)` is the black hold; `t_epoch_wait` precedes it". Example (t_epoch = 4 ms [UNV], one poll frame, t_epoch_wait = 16.7): "`restart_ms = 1 × 19.7 + 16.7 + max(6.1, 120) = 156.4 ms` ≤ 1 000 ✓ (hot copy: 16.7 + 16.7 + 120 = 153.4); worst case, two candidates refused: 3 × 19.7 + 16.7 + 120 = 59.1 + 16.7 + 120 = 195.8 ms; a Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation (no advance): 19.7 + 0 + 120 = 139.7 and 59.1 + 0 + 120 = 179.1; at the epoch timeout: 19.7 + 30 × 16.67 (= 500) + 120 = 639.7 ms ≤ 1 000 ✓". (J) Tuning knob row `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS`: too high -> "the pre-restore staging stretches (the held down-sheet frame, or the Continue screen) while a slow disk finishes the `slot_epoch.bin` write"; too low -> "the write is declared not durable (`SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, `save_status` `FAILED`) on a healthy slow disk; a kill before the next successful write replays that epoch once"; affects -> "SL-23 (2), (2a); T-8 step 2b; F-8 `t_epoch_wait`; monotonic ms". (K) Player Fantasy anchor step 4: "On that same tick's boundary the death stub requests a restore of the newest verified generation (the one from T = 437 400)" -> "On that same tick's boundary the death stub selects and stages the newest verified generation (the one from T = 437 400) and makes the new restore epoch durable; at the next boundary, one frame later, it requests the restore (R14)". Player Fantasy D16 note: "(... the epoch advances on every restore, death stub or load, and is durable before the first `RUNNING` tick; whether a Save & Quit followed by Continue should instead be exempt is a USER DECISION, OQ-50.)" -> "(R13/R14: a death-stub restore advances the epoch and makes it durable before the restore is requested; a Continue of the newest Save & Quit generation carries it, so quitting buys no re-key; OQ-50 closed.)" Game Feel 'then on the `DEAD` tick the stub restores' -> 'then the stub starts on the `DEAD` tick and restores one frame later'. (L) Edge Cases: 'Continue while LOADING' "one `restore_epoch` step" -> "at most one `restore_epoch` step (none for a Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation, R13)"; 'DEAD during a camera cut' "the request is made at that tick's boundary" -> "the stub starts at that tick's boundary and the request follows its epoch staging (R14)". (M) Every Interactions/Dependencies row quoting the epoch as a header value or the old signature conforms to the wording above. G3 confirming grep after the edit: `header-only|E_seen|SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE|end-of-.LOADING. hand-off|every restore advances|advances on every restore|in the generation headers` -> zero hits outside history markers.

requests.change: Rewrite the epoch criteria, metrics and open questions to R13/R14 (same names as the mechanism request). (1) AC-SL-142 -> "**AC-SL-142 (auto) — the epoch advances on a death restore, carries across Save & Quit, and is durable before the request** (R13, R14; user ruling D16). GIVEN a session saved by `save_and_quit()` at `T = 20 000` with `restore_epoch = e`, WHEN a fresh process Continues it (the newest non-demoted verified generation is that `QUIT` generation), THEN `slot_epoch.bin` is not written, `kernel.clock.restore_epoch` reads `e`, `restore_reason` reads `LOAD_GAME`, and the restored kernel and an uninterrupted control kernel at epoch `e`, run to `T = 21 000` on the same command stream, have equal `state_hash(PERSIST)`, equal persisted counters and seeds and identical threat draws (R13 (ii)); GIVEN a death-stub restore, THEN `slot_epoch.bin` reads `e + 1` with a valid CRC32 before `request_restore` is called (a spy records `EPOCH_DURABLE` then the request), `kernel.clock.restore_epoch` reads `e + 1`, `restore_reason` reads `DEATH_STUB` on the first `RUNNING` frame, and the post-restore threat draws differ from those at `e` (R13 (i); a step-back to an older generation included); between `DEAD` and the request the kernel stays `RUNNING`, the seat `DEAD`, and no snapshot or pause is requested; GIVEN a stub that finds nothing loadable, THEN the epoch did not advance and `slot_epoch.bin` was not written. Cites: SL-21, SL-23, T-8." (2) AC-SL-145 -> "(i) GIVEN one autosave restored by the death stub twice in one process, THEN epochs `e + 1`, `e + 2` and the kernel-derived draws (spy on `counter_eff`, same `rng_counter`) differ. (ii) GIVEN Save & Quit and Continue of that newest `QUIT` generation, in a fresh process, THEN the epoch is unchanged and the draws identical (see AC-SL-142); GIVEN the same `QUIT` generation not the newest (an `AUTO` written after it) or demoted, THEN the Continue of the selected generation advances it. requests.anchor: SL-23 "(2) *Durable before play.* Save/Load durably writes the new value into the header of the generation it restores, by an atomic header-only rewrite"
requests.change: Rewrite the epoch mechanism per delegated rulings R13/R14 (re-mark touched R1 text "delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14"; marker *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14)*; in-text record "Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14 (user delegated all remaining calls, including naming the reference machine)"). New names, used identically in every file: `slot_epoch.bin`, `slot_epoch.tmp`, `EPOCH_DURABLE`, `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` (replaces `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`), `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`, `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500, unchanged), `t_epoch_wait`. (A) SL-23 (1)-(5) replacement text: "(1) *Advance (R13).* A death-stub restore (`DEATH_STUB`) always advances `restore_epoch`. A Continue (`LOAD_GAME`, in-process or in a fresh process) or a `FAULT_RECOVERY` restore advances it unless the generation it restores is a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation; that Continue carries the epoch unchanged and writes nothing (user ruling D16, 'not steerable by quit', outranks R1). An advance sets `restore_epoch := min(2^32 − 1, max(e_mem, e_slot) + 1)`, `e_slot` the value in `slot_epoch.bin`, `e_mem` the in-memory value; at 2^32 − 1 it saturates and logs. A stub that finds nothing loadable restores nothing and does not advance it. (2) *Durable before the restore is requested (R14).* `restore_epoch` lives in the per-slot side file `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch.bin` (u32 little-endian + CRC32, 8 bytes), written by the Save/Load worker atomically (`slot_epoch.tmp`, flush, rename over, re-read with a valid CRC = `EPOCH_DURABLE`). It is in no generation file, so no generation's bytes, trailer SHA-256 or any key derived from them (SL-12) ever change after `VERIFYING`. When an advance is due, Save/Load runs a pre-restore staging step: after selection, pre-check and staging (SL-8, SL-11) it hands the new value to the worker, polls once per frame (never blocking the main thread), and calls `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`; the kernel's `LOADING` stays atomic within one boundary service. For the death stub the kernel keeps running between the `DEAD` boundary and that call (`t_epoch_wait`, F-8, typically one frame): the seat stays `DEAD`, the hard gate is closed (a seat `DEAD`, a restore pending), Save/Load issues no snapshot and no pause, the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame, and every tick of that interval is discarded by the restore. For a Continue the staging runs behind the Continue press, before the kernel is touched. (2a) *Failure path, a listed exposure.* If the write fails or `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` passes, the restore proceeds with the advanced value in memory, `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` is logged and `save_status` is set to `FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway); the worker re-attempts the `slot_epoch.bin` write with the next write job; a kill before a later successful write may replay that epoch once (OQ-25). (2b) *Recovery copy.* Each generation header records the live `restore_epoch` at write time (SL-1) and is never rewritten. A missing `slot_epoch.bin`, or one failing its CRC32, reads as `max(the newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`, and is rewritten at the next advance. `new_game` writes `slot_epoch.bin` = 0 (SL-18)." (3) keeps its content with the new signature. (4) unchanged. (5) -> "the player can neither pick nor predict the new value; a death re-keys the next stretch (metric M2); a Save & Quit then Continue carries the epoch, so the threat draws after Continue are those the quitting session would have met — quit buys no re-key (R13; OQ-50 closed); a kill then Continue of an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation advances it, priced by the minutes lost since that autosave (OQ-25). The former rules 'advances on a death-stub restore only' and 'every restore advances it' are superseded." Delete "is a key of every generation header (SL-1), so it survives ...", every `E_seen` definition and use, and the whole header-only rewrite / end-of-`LOADING` `EPOCH_DURABLE` wait text. Wall-clock paragraph: add `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` to the monotonic I/O timeouts and note it is the one that runs while `T` advances (the dead-world interval of the death stub), changing no sim state. (B) States intro: "which is persisted in the generation headers (SL-23)" -> "which is persisted in `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-23, R14), with a write-time copy in each generation header".
